Timber-frame engineering reference and review gates

Primary project reference: TFEC 1-2019, Standard for Design of Timber Frame Structures and Commentary, the latest TFEC 1 edition verified in the publisher catalogue on November 2, 2026. This is a design-review basis, not a compliance or construction approval.

TFEC §1.1: NDS prevails in conflicts. The applicable jurisdiction, adopted code/NDS edition and engineer of record are not yet established. An existing building or a geometrically fitting model does not establish this reconstruction's capacity.

  • Confirm species, grade, moisture, actual sections, design loads and support conditions.
  • For every joint family, record intended forces, bearing and positive retention, reduced-section checks, evidence and reviewer disposition.
  • After any joint edit, recompute volumes, centroids, contact areas, warning anchors and restraint classifications; rerun fit and regression checks.
  • Complete member, connection, lateral-load path, foundation, serviceability and erection checks with qualified structural review before fabrication.

Red arrows remain applied timber self-weight only. Reactions, pressure demands, strain and capacities remain unsolved. Proposed step-lap geometry is available in the main model selector. Connection design and fabrication review remain unresolved.

Applied timber self-weight only; not solved stresses/reactions or structural approval. Unflagged does not mean safe.

Illustrative species/moisture scenarios, not measured material. Partially cured does not establish moisture content. Assumes green-volume conditions; density = 1000 × basic specific gravity × (1 + MC/100). USDA density basis · Species data, Table 5–3.

Red arrows act downward at net-volume centroids. Width uses a square-root force scale (N/lbf), not pressure; glyph lengths are illustrative. X-ray overlay: arrows are not occluded by wood. Only visible timber arrows are drawn; total includes all 104 timbers. In top view, downward arrows appear edge-on and may disappear; that does not mean zero weight.

Excludes plywood, steel, roof/wall finishes, occupants, snow and wind. No reactions, strain, deflection or safety factor have been solved.

Geometry basis & joint status
How to read the angles

Axis inclination describes the member’s direction. Cut-plane angles are measured from the member axis; they are not saw settings.

Inside edge angles pass through timber material; over 180° identifies a concave corner. The acute plane angle is the smaller angle between the adjacent planes.

R01 A/B references describe the revised member ends. The conditional 22.5° miter assumes an equal regular-octagon ring. Neither establishes a construction joint. Saved axis/end reference angles are retained on proposed members and are not a complete proposed cut schedule; mesh-edge angles describe the selected actual surfaces.
